attacks.claim: In dark mode `.day-card` keeps a hardcoded white background while `color: var(--text)` flips to near-white (#f2f2f7), so planner text is nearly invisible on cards for ~30% of users. It ships to 100% and QA covered only light mode.
attacks.evidence: .day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... } with @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --text: #f2f2f7; ... } }; QA: "Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light)"

attacks.claim: On mobile the fixed 72px action bar has no reserved bottom space on `.planner` (only 16px padding), so the last day (Sunday) and its Swap/overflow buttons can be covered and unreachable.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; ... bottom: 0; height: 72px; } and .planner { ... padding: 16px; ... }; "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: The tile image is 320px wide with no CSS constraint such as max-width:100%. At 360px viewport, content width after page and card padding is ~296px, so the image can overflow the card on the primary mobile widths.
attacks.evidence: ; ABSENT: any `.tile img { max-width: 100%; height: auto }` rule

attacks.claim: The one-tap '+ List' is removed for the most frequent planner action (9.4/week per WAU, 64% mobile), replacing it with a ~5-6 step flow. The declutter rationale is not reconciled with the usage data, and no usability or funnel evidence supports the tradeoff.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level \"+ List\" button is removed to declutter tiles." / "tap the tile → recipe page → \"Ingredients\" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → \"Add to list\" → toast with \"Undo\""

attacks.claim: QA does not match actual traffic. 68% of sessions are 360-414px mobile and 30% dark mode, but visual QA ran only in light mode at 1440px desktop and iPhone 14. No 360px, dark-mode, touch-drag, or scrolled-to-bottom check was run.
attacks.evidence: "Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass"; ABSENT: dark-mode, 360px, touch drag evidence

attacks.claim: The 100% same-day ship has no staged ramp and no numeric thresholds or rollback triggers on the watched metrics. The flag-off fallback depends on ad hoc judgment during an incident.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`"; "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: 'Generate shopping list' bulk-adds all planned recipes with no described confirmation, dedupe, partial-failure handling, or undo. Undo is described only for the single-recipe add.
attacks.evidence: "\"Generate shopping list\" (adds all planned recipes for the week)"; undo only in single add flow

attacks.claim: The new 'Share plan' action exposes a user's weekly plan externally, but the artifact does not specify what is shared, link access model, expiry, or revocation.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: sharing scope, link token/access model, expiry, revocation. Only: "\"Share plan\"" in the action bar.

attacks.claim: Repeated 'Swap' buttons have no accessible name identifying their recipe, unlike the labelled overflow button, so they are ambiguous for screen-reader users across up to 21 tiles. The toast also has no specified live region.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button>; ABSENT: aria-live / role=status for the toast

attacks.claim: The rollback claim is asserted without stating that old and new markup/CSS are both retained and flag-selected, and without flag-off test evidence.
attacks.evidence: "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)"
